title: Pure Data
lede: A working diagram. The interface makes the program’s structure visible.
summary: Object boxes, patch cords, and a visible flow of information.

evidence.note: Official manual and patch image reviewed; application not run.

styles.note: The program is a diagram; its construction stays visible.

context: Pure Data (Pd) is a graphical programming environment for real-time audio, with multimedia extensions. Patches connect objects through visible inlets, outlets, and cords. [Official overview](https://msp.ucsd.edu/Pd_documentation/2.theory.of.operation.htm#s2.1).
observed: Small rectangular boxes carry monospaced object names.
Dark lines connect ports on a white canvas.
The patch reads as a chain of operations; geometry carries meaning.
The drawing has little decoration beyond the working elements.
borrow: Show relationships directly. Keep component boundaries and names visible. Let a useful diagram become the interface.
This interpretation describes the documented patch aesthetic; custom patches and extensions can look different.

images.alt: A Pure Data patch connecting notein to stripnote, mtof, osc~, a gain multiplier, and dac~ with dark patch cords.
images.caption: “A simple MIDI synthesizer,” figure 2.1.14 in the [official Pd manual](https://msp.ucsd.edu/Pd_documentation/2.theory.of.operation.htm#s2.1.2).
